newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool markets steady in high offering.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool markets steady in high offering.

text.p: The wool buying trade was heartened by a steadying trend in the Australian wool market this week, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said on Friday.
Despite the relatively high offering of 96,000 bales for this time of season, eastern market indicators were little changed over the week, it said in its market review.
The western market indicators provided by Wool International (WI) and the Australian Wool Exchange (AWEX) both reflected a correction consistent with that experienced in the east last week, it said.
The WI eastern market indicator firmed by seven cents to 703 cents a kilogram clear and the WI western market indicator fell 17 cents to 647 cents a kg clean.
A total of 95,978 bales on a WI basis were offered nationally with a passed in rate of 10 percent. The pass in rate over eastern markets was 7.7 percent and 14.4 percent in the west, it said.
Interest from European and Japanese sources remained quiet, but purchases for China and India provided good support.
Apart from the step correction in the west, market strength was relatively uniform across the week, firming to some extent from a soft start, it said.
There was sufficient strength in the market to offset the further appreciation of the Australian dollar, it said.
"It is felt that the current price level has found acceptance and the firm market is expected to continue next week with a lower quantity being offered," it said.
In its market weekly, WI said it had sold a provisional total of 16,018 farm bale equivalents in the week to August 14. At this date the WI stockpile of unsold wool totalled 1,505,575 bales, it said.
In futures, a total of 106 micron 21 contracts were sold in the week to August 14. Open interest decreased by 63 contracts to close at 1,290.
The August 1997 contract closed 19 cents down at 843 cents a kilogram clean. The October 1997 contract closed one cent up at 846 cents a kg clean.
A total of 79,445 bales are rostered for sale next week in Sydney and Melbourne.
